newsitem.title: USA: Digital prices workstations to compete.
newsitem.headline: Digital prices workstations to compete.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp has priced its new line of workstation computers based on its Alpha chips and which run on Windows NT operating system at more competitive levels to try to grab a larger share of the market, an executive with the company said.

The 64-bit Alpha systems are priced less than 10 percent more than the slower workstations using Intel Corp's Pentium Pro processors, Digital vice president of workstations Philippe Ribeyre told Reuters.
"It's very clear that the world, for the next few years, is going to be driven by Windows NT platforms. The Windows NT workstation market is expected to grow something like 40 percent," Ribeyre said.
About 70 percent of the 50,000 personal workstation computers based on Microsoft Corp's Windows NT which Digital has shipped over the last 18 months have used Intel chips, he said.
The remaining 30 percent have used Alpha, but he said he expected Alpha sales to grow with the release of the second generation of workstations on Wednesday.
"It offers extremely effective pricing," he said. "The price is very close to what you will find within the PC market."

Prices of Digital's personal workstation 433a start at $4995, with 64 megabytes of RAM memory adn Matrox graphics. The Digital Personal Workstation 500a, with 64 MB of RAM adn AccelPro 2500 graphics, is priced under $10,000, Digital said.
